headline: Germany's research ministry has advanced six teams of companies and universities in a competition offering up to €640 million for error-correcting quantum computers.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a national funding contest with a stated sum, deadline and named teams, confirmed by a selected company; only a first-stage selection.
importance_line: Researchers and engineers on the six teams, and firms such as the Munich start-up planqc, which leads a neutral-atom team, stay in the running for state funding, but €640 million is a ceiling and only the outline stage has been passed.
source: Quantum Computing Report, citing a planqc press release
summary: According to Quantum Computing Report, Germany's research ministry has advanced six teams in a competition offering up to €640 million ($717 million) for at least two fault-tolerant quantum computers, machines that can correct their own errors, by 2030. Two teams were picked for each of three ways of building qubits, the basic units of a quantum computer (neutral atoms, trapped ions and superconducting circuits), and all must show working entry systems by 31 Mar 2027.
